author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Australian shares closed at their lowest level in more than two months Friday as a sharp decline in mining companies outweighed gains in financial stocks. The S&P/ASX 200 ended 0.9% lower at 8,741.20, its weakest close since July 2, according to Reuters.

The benchmark lost 2.1% for the week, its steepest weekly decline since mid-March. Mining stocks fell 3.7%, with BHP down 4.1% and Rio Tinto down 3.5%. Lithium producers were also hit: Liontown Resources dropped 8.6% and PLS fell 7.4%. These are closing figures from Friday’s session, not live prices.

Investors were balancing commodity-company weakness against higher energy costs and rising interest-rate expectations. Oil above $100 a barrel added to concern that inflation could remain elevated. Australian government bond yields moved above 5%, their highest level since mid-2011, increasing the pressure on rate-sensitive valuations.

Financial shares provided a partial offset, gaining 1.1%. The split session showed how the current oil and bond-market shock can affect sectors differently: banks may benefit from parts of the rate environment, while resource shares remain exposed to commodity demand, currency moves and shifts in global risk appetite.
dek: The S&P/ASX 200 ended Friday down 0.9%, with mining stocks leading losses as elevated oil prices and bond yields weighed on sentiment.
headline: Australian shares close at two-month low as miners retreat
